records.literal_gloss: For the director. A maskil of the sons of Korah.

en.L: For the director: a maskil of the sons of Korah.
en.B: For the music director. A maskil of the sons of Korah.
en.R: For the leader of the music. A song of the family of Korah, to teach and give insight.

fr.L: Au chef de chœur : un maskil des fils de Coré.
fr.B: Au chef de chœur. Maskil des fils de Coré.
fr.R: Pour le chef des musiciens. Un chant de la famille de Coré, pour enseigner et faire comprendre.

sw.L: Kwa kiongozi wa kwaya: maskili ya wana wa Kora.
sw.B: Kwa kiongozi wa kwaya. Maskili ya wana wa Kora.
sw.R: Kwa kiongozi wa waimbaji. Wimbo wa ukoo wa Kora, wa kufundisha na kutoa ufahamu.

es.L: Al director del coro: un masquil de los hijos de Coré.
es.B: Al director del coro. Un masquil de los hijos de Coré.
es.R: Para el director de la música. Un canto de la familia de Coré, para enseñar y dar entendimiento.

vi.L: Cho người chỉ huy [ban nhạc]: [một] bài Mát-kin của con cháu Cô-ra.
vi.B: Cho nhạc trưởng. Bài Mát-kin của con cháu Cô-ra.
vi.R: Cho người hướng dẫn ban nhạc. Bài ca của dòng họ Cô-ra, để dạy dỗ và giúp hiểu biết.

decisions.choice: The title is verse 1
decisions.reason: The title is part of the Hebrew text and is counted as verse 1, so the verse numbers here are one higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: the director
decisions.reason: As in 4:1.

decisions.choice: maskil: a song of insight, or a skillful song
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb "to have insight, act wisely" (41:2). As a heading for thirteen psalms it may mark a song that teaches, or one composed with skill; its exact sense is no longer known.

decisions.choice: the sons of Korah: a guild of temple singers
decisions.reason: The descendants of Korah, a Levite (Numbers 26:11), served as singers in the temple (2 Chronicles 20:19). Psalms 42-49 and 84-88 bear their name.

decisions.choice: Psalms 42 and 43 are one poem
decisions.reason: The two psalms share a refrain (42:6, 42:12, 43:5) and the line "Why do I go about mourning ..." (42:10; 43:2), and Psalm 43 has no title, so they were first one song. Psalm 42 also opens Book Two of the Psalms (Psalms 42-72).

decisions.choice: a song of the family of Korah, to teach and give insight
alternatives: a maskil of the sons of Korah
decisions.reason: Readable gives the likely sense of maskil (m2) and says what "sons" means here.

decisions.choice: "wana wa Kora" (L, B); "ukoo wa Kora" (the family of Korah) at Readable
decisions.reason: The sons of Korah were a guild of temple singers descended from Korah; Readable says "ukoo" (clan, family line), as the English Readable says "the family of Korah".

decisions.choice: los hijos de Coré
decisions.reason: The sons of Korah, a guild of temple singers, are "los hijos de Coré" at Literal and Balanced, with the usual Spanish form of the name; Readable says "la familia de Coré", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "con cháu Cô-ra" (L, B); "dòng họ Cô-ra" (R)
decisions.reason: The sons of Korah were a family guild of temple singers (see the meaning decision), so "con cháu" (descendants) fits better than "con trai"; Readable says "family", as the English Readable does.

source.text: כְּאַיָּ֗ל תַּעֲרֹ֥ג עַל־אֲפִֽיקֵי־מָ֑יִם כֵּ֤ן נַפְשִׁ֨י תַעֲרֹ֖ג אֵלֶ֣יךָ אֱלֹהִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: As a deer longs for channels of water, so my soul longs for you, God.

en.L: As a deer longs for channels of water, so my soul longs for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, God.
en.B: Like a doe that longs for running streams, I long for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, God, with all my being.
en.R: A deer is thirsty and looks for a stream of water. In the same way, God, I am longing for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

fr.L: Comme une biche soupire après des cours d’eau, ainsi mon âme soupire après {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, ô Dieu.
fr.B: Comme la biche qui languit après les ruisseaux d’eau vive, je languis après {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, ô Dieu, de tout mon être.
fr.R: Une biche a soif et cherche un ruisseau. De la même façon, ô Dieu, je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} désire de tout mon cœur.

sw.L: Kama kulungu anavyotamani vijito vya maji, ndivyo nafsi yangu inavyokutamani {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, Mungu.
sw.B: Kama paa jike anavyovitamani vijito vya maji yanayotiririka, ndivyo ninavyokutamani {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, Mungu, kwa nafsi yangu yote.
sw.R: Kulungu akiwa na kiu hutafuta kijito cha maji. Vivyo hivyo, Mungu, ninakutamani {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}.

es.L: Como un ciervo suspira por los cauces de agua, así suspira mi alma por {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, oh Dios.
es.B: Como la cierva que ansía los arroyos que corren, así {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} anhelo yo, oh Dios, con todo mi ser.
es.R: Un ciervo tiene sed y busca un arroyo de agua. Así mismo, Dios, yo tengo ansias de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}.

vi.L: Như con nai khao khát những dòng nước, linh hồn tôi cũng khao khát {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} như vậy, lạy Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.B: Như nai cái mong mỏi những dòng suối chảy, lạy Đức Chúa Trời, tôi cũng hết lòng khao khát {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} như vậy.
vi.R: Con nai khát nước và đi tìm dòng suối. Cũng vậy, lạy Đức Chúa Trời, tôi đang khao khát {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

decisions.choice: longs: cries out with thirst
decisions.reason: The verb ('arag) is found only here and in Joel 1:20, where animals cry out to God for water in a drought. It is longing that can be heard.

decisions.choice: a deer: perhaps a doe
decisions.reason: The noun is masculine but the verb is feminine, so the animal may be a doe.

decisions.choice: my soul: my whole self, thirsting
decisions.reason: Nefesh can also mean the throat; the picture of thirst is felt in the whole person.

decisions.choice: God: the name used in Book Two
decisions.reason: In Psalms 42-83 the general word for God ('elohim) is used far more often than the divine name. Psalm 42 uses the name only once (verse 9).

decisions.choice: I (with all my being)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "I" for nefesh here, as the convention allows.

source.text: צָמְאָ֬ה נַפְשִׁ֨י׀לֵאלֹהִים֮ לְאֵ֪ל חָ֥י מָתַ֥י אָב֑וֹא וְ֝אֵרָאֶ֗ה פְּנֵ֣י אֱלֹהִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: My soul thirsts for God, for [the] God living; when will I come and appear [before] the face of God?

en.L: My soul thirsts for God, for the living God; when will I come and appear before the face of God?
en.B: I am thirsty for God, the living God. When may I come and stand before God's face?
en.R: I am thirsty for God, the God who is alive. When can I go to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} house and be with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} again?

fr.L: Mon âme a soif de Dieu, du Dieu vivant ; quand viendrai-je et paraîtrai-je devant la face de Dieu ?
fr.B: J’ai soif de Dieu, du Dieu vivant. Quand pourrai-je venir me présenter devant la face de Dieu ?
fr.R: J’ai soif de Dieu, du Dieu qui est vivant. Quand pourrai-je aller dans {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} maison et être de nouveau avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ?

sw.L: Nafsi yangu inamwonea kiu Mungu, Mungu aliye hai; nitakuja lini na kuonekana mbele ya uso wa Mungu?
sw.B: Nina kiu ya Mungu, Mungu aliye hai. Nitakuja lini nisimame mbele za uso wa Mungu?
sw.R: Nina kiu ya Mungu, Mungu aliye hai. Nitaweza lini kwenda nyumbani {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}} na kuwa pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} tena?

es.L: Mi alma tiene sed de Dios, del Dios vivo; ¿cuándo vendré y me presentaré ante el rostro de Dios?
es.B: Tengo sed de Dios, del Dios vivo. ¿Cuándo podré ir y estar delante del rostro de Dios?
es.R: Tengo sed de Dios, del Dios que está vivo. ¿Cuándo podré ir a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} casa y estar con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} otra vez?

vi.L: Linh hồn tôi khát Đức Chúa Trời, Đức Chúa Trời hằng sống; khi nào tôi sẽ đến và ra mắt trước mặt Đức Chúa Trời?
vi.B: Tôi khát Đức Chúa Trời, Đức Chúa Trời hằng sống. Bao giờ tôi được đến và đứng trước mặt Đức Chúa Trời?
vi.R: Tôi khát khao Đức Chúa Trời, Đức Chúa Trời đang sống. Bao giờ tôi mới được đến nhà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và lại ở với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}?

decisions.choice: the living God
decisions.reason: God ('el) who is alive and acts, unlike idols (84:3; Joshua 3:10). The thirst is for God himself, as living water (Jeremiah 2:13).

decisions.choice: appear before the face of God
decisions.reason: The vowels of the Hebrew text read "appear before", the phrase used for coming to the sanctuary at the festivals (Exodus 23:17; Deuteronomy 16:16). The same letters could be read "see the face of God", and some ancient translations do so. The meaning is close: to come into God's presence in his house.

decisions.choice: to his house
decisions.reason: Readable says where one appears before God's face (m2).

source.text: הָֽיְתָה־לִּ֬י דִמְעָתִ֣י לֶ֭חֶם יוֹמָ֣ם וָלָ֑יְלָה בֶּאֱמֹ֥ר אֵלַ֥י כָּל־הַ֝יּ֗וֹם אַיֵּ֥ה אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: My tears have been to me [my] bread by day and night, while [they] say to me all the day, Where [is] your God?

en.L: My tears have been my bread by day and night, while [they] say to me all the day, "Where [is] your God?"
en.B: Day and night I have fed on my tears, while all day long people ask me, "Where is your God?"
en.R: I cry all day and all night; tears are all I have to eat. All day long people ask me, "Where is your God?"

fr.L: Mes larmes ont été mon pain jour et nuit, tandis qu’[on] me dit tout le jour : « Où [est] ton Dieu ? »
fr.B: Jour et nuit je me suis nourri de mes larmes, pendant que toute la journée on me demande : « Où est ton Dieu ? »
fr.R: Je pleure jour et nuit ; les larmes sont ma seule nourriture. Toute la journée, les gens me demandent : « Où est ton Dieu ? »

sw.L: Machozi yangu yamekuwa chakula changu mchana na usiku, huku [wakiniambia] mchana kutwa, "Mungu wako [yuko] wapi?"
sw.B: Mchana na usiku nimejilisha machozi yangu, huku watu wakiniuliza mchana kutwa, "Mungu wako yuko wapi?"
sw.R: Ninalia mchana wote na usiku wote; machozi ndiyo chakula changu pekee. Mchana kutwa watu wananiuliza, "Mungu wako yuko wapi?"

es.L: Mis lágrimas han sido mi pan de día y de noche, mientras me dicen todo el día: «¿Dónde [está] tu Dios?».
es.B: Día y noche me he alimentado de mis lágrimas, mientras todo el día la gente me pregunta: «¿Dónde está tu Dios?».
es.R: Lloro todo el día y toda la noche; las lágrimas son lo único que tengo para comer. Todo el día la gente me pregunta: «¿Dónde está tu Dios?».

vi.L: Nước mắt tôi đã thành bánh của tôi ngày và đêm, trong khi [người ta] suốt ngày nói với tôi: "Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi [ở] đâu?"
vi.B: Ngày đêm tôi lấy nước mắt làm thức ăn, trong khi suốt ngày người ta hỏi tôi: "Đức Chúa Trời của anh ở đâu?"
vi.R: Tôi khóc suốt ngày suốt đêm; nước mắt là thức ăn duy nhất của tôi. Suốt ngày người ta hỏi tôi: "Đức Chúa Trời của anh đâu rồi?"

decisions.choice: my tears have been my bread: I have wept instead of eating
decisions.reason: His grief is so great that tears are his only food (80:6; 102:10).

decisions.choice: Where is your God?: a mocking question
decisions.reason: People ask it to mock, as if his God had left him or did not exist (79:10; 115:2).

decisions.choice: the mockers say "ngươi" (L) and "anh" (B, R) for "your"
decisions.reason: The question is a mocking one (see the meaning decision); Literal uses the old contemptuous "ngươi", while Balanced and Readable use "anh", how people speak to a man as an equal, which keeps the scorn in the question itself.

source.text: אֵ֤לֶּה אֶזְכְּרָ֨ה׀וְאֶשְׁפְּכָ֬ה עָלַ֨י׀נַפְשִׁ֗י כִּ֤י אֶֽעֱבֹ֨ר׀בַּסָּךְ֮ אֶדַּדֵּ֗ם עַד־בֵּ֥ית אֱלֹ֫הִ֥ים בְּקוֹל־רִנָּ֥ה וְתוֹדָ֗ה הָמ֥וֹן חוֹגֵֽג׃

records.literal_gloss: These I remember, and I pour out on me my soul: that I used to pass along with the throng; I led them in procession to [the] house of God, with [the] sound of a joyful shout and thanksgiving, a multitude keeping festival.

en.L: These [things] I remember, and I pour out my soul within me: how I used to go along with the throng, leading them in procession to the house of God, with the sound of a joyful shout and thanksgiving, a multitude keeping festival.
en.B: I pour out my heart as I call these things to mind: how I walked with the crowd and led them up to God's house, among shouts of joy and songs of thanks, a great crowd celebrating the feast.
en.R: My heart breaks when I remember how things used to be. I used to walk with the crowds to God's house. I led them as they went. We shouted for joy and sang songs of thanks. A huge crowd was celebrating the festival.

fr.L: De ces [choses] je me souviens, et je répands mon âme au-dedans de moi : comment j’allais avec la foule, la conduisant en procession jusqu’à la maison de Dieu, au son des cris de joie et de l’action de grâce, une multitude en fête.
fr.B: Je laisse déborder mon cœur quand je me rappelle tout cela : je marchais avec la foule et je la menais jusqu’à la maison de Dieu, parmi les cris de joie et les chants de reconnaissance, une grande foule célébrant la fête.
fr.R: Mon cœur se brise quand je me souviens de ce qui se passait avant. Je marchais avec la foule vers la maison de Dieu. Je la conduisais. Nous poussions des cris de joie et nous chantions pour dire merci. Une foule immense célébrait la fête.

sw.L: Mambo haya ninayakumbuka, na kuimimina nafsi yangu ndani yangu: jinsi nilivyokuwa nikienda pamoja na umati, nikiwaongoza katika maandamano hadi nyumba ya Mungu, kwa sauti ya kelele za furaha na shukrani, umati ukishika sikukuu.
sw.B: Ninaumimina moyo wangu ninapoyakumbuka mambo haya: jinsi nilivyotembea pamoja na umati na kuwaongoza kupanda hadi nyumba ya Mungu, katikati ya kelele za furaha na nyimbo za shukrani, umati mkubwa ukisherehekea sikukuu.
sw.R: Moyo wangu unavunjika ninapokumbuka jinsi mambo yalivyokuwa zamani. Nilikuwa nikitembea pamoja na umati kwenda nyumbani kwa Mungu. Niliwaongoza walipokuwa wakienda. Tulipiga kelele za furaha na kuimba nyimbo za shukrani. Umati mkubwa ulikuwa ukisherehekea sikukuu.

es.L: Estas [cosas] recuerdo, y derramo mi alma dentro de mí: cómo yo pasaba con la multitud, guiándola en procesión a la casa de Dios, con voz de grito alegre y de acción de gracias, una muchedumbre en fiesta.
es.B: Desahogo mi corazón al traer estas cosas a la memoria: cómo caminaba con la multitud y la guiaba hasta la casa de Dios, entre gritos de alegría y cantos de gratitud, una gran muchedumbre que celebraba la fiesta.
es.R: Se me parte el corazón cuando recuerdo cómo eran las cosas antes. Yo caminaba con la gente hacia la casa de Dios. Yo los guiaba mientras iban. Gritábamos de alegría y cantábamos canciones de gratitud. Una enorme multitud celebraba la fiesta.

vi.L: Những [điều] này tôi nhớ lại, và tôi dốc đổ linh hồn tôi trong tôi: thể nào tôi từng đi cùng đoàn người, dẫn họ đi rước đến nhà Đức Chúa Trời, với tiếng reo mừng và cảm tạ, một đám đông giữ lễ.
vi.B: Tôi dốc đổ nỗi lòng khi nhớ lại những điều này: thể nào tôi đã đi cùng đoàn người và dẫn họ lên nhà Đức Chúa Trời, giữa tiếng reo vui và những bài ca cảm tạ, một đám đông đang mừng lễ.
vi.R: Lòng tôi tan nát khi nhớ lại những ngày trước. Tôi từng đi cùng đoàn người đông đảo đến nhà Đức Chúa Trời. Tôi dẫn đầu khi họ đi. Chúng tôi reo vui và hát những bài ca cảm tạ. Cả một đám đông đang mừng lễ.

decisions.choice: I pour out my soul: I let all my grief out
decisions.reason: To pour out the soul or the heart is to spill out one's grief before God (62:9; 1 Samuel 1:15).

decisions.choice: the throng; I led them in procession
alternatives: in the shelter (of the Mighty One)
decisions.reason: Both words are rare. The first (sakh) seems to mean a crowd; the second (eddaddem) seems to mean leading or walking with them at a festival pace. The ancient Greek translation read the line quite differently.

decisions.choice: a multitude keeping festival: the pilgrim feasts
decisions.reason: Three times a year Israel went up to the sanctuary for the feasts (Deuteronomy 16:16). The verb (chagag) is to keep such a festival with joy.

decisions.choice: My heart breaks
decisions.reason: Readable gives the feeling behind the picture (m1).

source.text: מַה־תִּשְׁתּ֬וֹחֲחִ֨י׀נַפְשִׁי֮ וַתֶּהֱמִ֪י עָ֫לָ֥י הוֹחִ֣ילִי לֵֽ֭אלֹהִים כִּי־ע֥וֹד אוֹדֶ֗נּוּ יְשׁוּע֥וֹת פָּנָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: Why are you bowed down, my soul, and you are in turmoil within me? Wait for God, for I will yet give thanks to him [for the] salvation of his face.

en.L: Why are you bowed down, my soul, and [why] are you in turmoil within me? Wait for God, for I will yet give thanks to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, [for] the salvation of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face.
en.B: Why are you bent so low, my soul? Why this unrest inside me? Wait for God in hope; I will give {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} thanks again, for the rescue that comes from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence.
en.R: I tell myself: Why are you so sad? Why are you so upset? Keep hoping in God! I will praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} again. When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is with me, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saves me.

fr.L: Pourquoi es-tu abattue, mon âme, et [pourquoi] gémis-tu au-dedans de moi ? Espère en Dieu, car je {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} louerai encore, [pour] le salut de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} face.
fr.B: Pourquoi es-tu si abattue, mon âme ? Pourquoi ce trouble au-dedans de moi ? Espère en Dieu ; je {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} rendrai grâce encore, pour le salut qui vient de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} présence.
fr.R: Je me dis : Pourquoi es-tu si triste ? Pourquoi es-tu si inquiet ? Continue d’espérer en Dieu ! Je {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} louerai encore. Quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est avec moi, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} me sauve.

sw.L: Mbona umeinama, nafsi yangu, na mbona unafadhaika ndani yangu? Mngojee Mungu, kwa maana bado nitamshukuru {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}, [kwa] wokovu wa uso {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.
sw.B: Mbona umeinama hivyo, nafsi yangu? Mbona huku kuhangaika ndani yangu? Mngojee Mungu kwa tumaini; nitamshukuru tena, kwa wokovu unaotoka mbele {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}.
sw.R: Ninajiambia: Mbona una huzuni hivyo? Mbona umefadhaika hivyo? Endelea kumtumaini Mungu! Nitamsifu tena. Akiwa pamoja nami, huniokoa.

es.L: ¿Por qué estás abatida, alma mía, y [por qué] te turbas dentro de mí? Espera en Dios, porque aún {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} daré gracias, [por] la salvación de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} rostro.
es.B: ¿Por qué te doblegas tanto, alma mía? ¿Por qué esta inquietud dentro de mí? Espera en Dios con esperanza; otra vez {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} daré gracias, por el rescate que viene de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} presencia.
es.R: Me digo a mí mismo: ¿Por qué estás tan triste? ¿Por qué estás tan preocupado? ¡Sigue esperando en Dios! Otra vez {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} alabaré. Cuando {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} está conmigo, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} me salva.

vi.L: Hỡi linh hồn tôi, sao lại cúi rạp xuống, và sao lại xao xuyến trong tôi? Hãy trông đợi Đức Chúa Trời, vì tôi sẽ còn cảm tạ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, [vì] sự cứu rỗi của mặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Hỡi linh hồn tôi, sao lại gục ngã đến thế? Sao lại bồn chồn trong tôi? Hãy hy vọng nơi Đức Chúa Trời; tôi sẽ lại cảm tạ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, vì sự giải cứu đến từ sự hiện diện của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Tôi tự nhủ: Sao lại buồn đến thế? Sao lại bối rối đến thế? Hãy cứ hy vọng nơi Đức Chúa Trời! Tôi sẽ lại ca ngợi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ở với tôi, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cứu tôi.

decisions.choice: my soul: the psalmist speaks to himself
decisions.reason: The refrain is a conversation inside the psalmist: one part of him asks why his soul is so low and urges it to hope. Soul (nefesh) is the whole self, here his own heart.

decisions.choice: bowed down, in turmoil: crushed and restless
decisions.reason: The first verb (shachach) is to be bent low, sunk down; the second (hamah) is the roaring or restlessness of the sea, which the poem pictures in 42:8.

decisions.choice: the salvation of his face
alternatives: the salvation of my face, and my God (as in 42:12 and 43:5)
decisions.reason: Here the Hebrew text has "the salvation of his face", that is, the help that comes from God's presence. In the other two refrains it reads "the salvation of my face, and my God". Some Hebrew manuscripts and ancient translations read the refrain here as there, joining "my God" from the start of verse 7. The Hebrew text as it stands is followed.

decisions.choice: why
decisions.reason: The second "why" of the other refrains is not repeated here; it is understood (bracketed at Literal).

decisions.choice: I tell myself: Why are you ...
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that he is speaking to himself (m1).

decisions.choice: the psalmist speaks to his soul with "tu"; "mon âme" (feminine) at Literal and Balanced, so "abattue"; at Readable he speaks to himself ("Je me dis"), so "triste", "inquiet"
decisions.reason: The refrain (here, 42:12 and 43:5) is the psalmist talking to himself. Literal and Balanced keep nefesh as "mon âme", and French adjectives agree with it; Readable, as the English, makes it plain that he speaks to himself, and the adjectives follow the speaker.

decisions.choice: the refrain of 42:6, 42:12 and 43:5 in the same Swahili words each time; Readable opens with "Ninajiambia" (I tell myself)
decisions.reason: The psalmist talks to his own "nafsi"; Swahili can address the soul as "you" just as Hebrew does. The three refrains are kept word for word alike, so that readers hear the poem's repeated cry, and Readable says plainly that he is speaking to himself, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: alma mía
decisions.reason: The psalmist speaks to his own soul (nefesh). Spanish puts the possessive after the noun in an address, "alma mía", and the feminine "abatida" agrees with "alma"; Readable makes the self-talk plain, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: the singer speaks to his soul with no pronoun: "Hỡi linh hồn tôi, sao lại ...?"
decisions.reason: He speaks to himself (see the meaning decision). Vietnamese has no neutral "you" for one's own soul: "ngươi" is old-fashioned and "mày" rough, so the question leaves the subject unspoken, which Vietnamese allows.

source.text: אֱֽלֹהַ֗י עָלַי֮ נַפְשִׁ֪י תִשְׁתּ֫וֹחָ֥ח עַל־כֵּ֗ן אֶ֭זְכָּרְךָ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ יַרְדֵּ֑ן וְ֝חֶרְמוֹנִ֗ים מֵהַ֥ר מִצְעָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: My God, within me my soul is bowed down; therefore I remember you from [the] land of Jordan and Hermons, from Mount Mizar.

en.L: My God, my soul is bowed down within me; therefore I remember {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} from the land of [the] Jordan and [the] Hermons, from Mount Mizar.
en.B: My God, I am bent low inside; so I will remember {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} here in the Jordan country and on the peaks of Hermon, on Mount Mizar.
en.R: My God, I feel so sad. So I think about {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} here, far away in the north, where the Jordan River begins, near Mount Hermon and Mount Mizar.

fr.L: Mon Dieu, mon âme est abattue au-dedans de moi ; c’est pourquoi je me souviens de {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} depuis le pays du Jourdain et des Hermon, depuis le mont Mitsar.
fr.B: Mon Dieu, je suis abattu au fond de moi ; alors je me souviendrai de {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, ici, au pays du Jourdain et sur les sommets de l’Hermon, sur le mont Mitsar.
fr.R: Mon Dieu, je suis si triste. Alors je pense à {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} ici, loin dans le nord, là où le Jourdain prend sa source, près du mont Hermon et du mont Mitsar.

sw.L: Mungu wangu, nafsi yangu imeinama ndani yangu; kwa hiyo ninakukumbuka {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} kutoka nchi ya Yordani na [milima ya] Hermoni, kutoka Mlima Mizari.
sw.B: Mungu wangu, nimeinama ndani yangu; kwa hiyo nitakukumbuka {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} hapa katika nchi ya Yordani na juu ya vilele vya Hermoni, juu ya Mlima Mizari.
sw.R: Mungu wangu, nina huzuni sana. Kwa hiyo ninakufikiria {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} hapa, mbali kaskazini, mahali Mto Yordani unapoanzia, karibu na Mlima Hermoni na Mlima Mizari.

es.L: Dios mío, mi alma está abatida dentro de mí; por eso me acuerdo de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} desde la tierra del Jordán y de los Hermones, desde el monte Mizar.
es.B: Dios mío, estoy abatido por dentro; por eso me acordaré de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} aquí en la región del Jordán y en las cumbres del Hermón, en el monte Mizar.
es.R: Dios mío, me siento muy triste. Por eso pienso en {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} aquí, lejos en el norte, donde nace el río Jordán, cerca del monte Hermón y del monte Mizar.

vi.L: Lạy Đức Chúa Trời của tôi, linh hồn tôi cúi rạp trong tôi; vì vậy tôi nhớ đến {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} từ đất Giô-đanh và [các ngọn] Hẹt-môn, từ núi Mít-sê-a.
vi.B: Lạy Đức Chúa Trời của tôi, lòng tôi gục ngã; vì vậy tôi sẽ nhớ đến {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} tại miền Giô-đanh này và trên các đỉnh Hẹt-môn, trên núi Mít-sê-a.
vi.R: Lạy Đức Chúa Trời của tôi, tôi buồn quá. Vì vậy tôi nghĩ đến {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} tại đây, xa tít miền bắc, nơi sông Giô-đanh bắt nguồn, gần núi Hẹt-môn và núi Mít-sê-a.

decisions.choice: the Jordan and the Hermons: far from Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The Jordan rises at the foot of Mount Hermon, in the far north of the land. The Hermons are its peaks. The poet is far from the temple, among the mountains and rushing water of the next verse.

decisions.choice: Mizar: a hill whose place is unknown
decisions.reason: The name means "little" and is otherwise unknown; it may be a small peak near Hermon, set against the great mountain.

decisions.choice: therefore I remember you: memory against despair
decisions.reason: Because he is low, he turns his mind to God, answering the refrain's question. "My God" at the start may belong to the end of verse 6 (see the note there).

decisions.choice: far away in the north
decisions.reason: Readable says where these places are (m1).

source.text: תְּהֽוֹם־אֶל־תְּה֣וֹם ק֭וֹרֵא לְק֣וֹל צִנּוֹרֶ֑יךָ כָּֽל־מִשְׁבָּרֶ֥יךָ וְ֝גַלֶּ֗יךָ עָלַ֥י עָבָֽרוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Deep to deep is calling at [the] sound of your waterfalls; all your breakers and your waves over me have passed.

en.L: Deep calls to deep at the sound of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} waterfalls; all {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} breakers and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} waves have passed over me.
en.B: One deep calls out to another at the roar of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} cascades; all {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} breaking waves and rollers have gone over my head.
en.R: Your waterfalls roar, and the deep waters call to each other. It is as if {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} waves are crashing over me, and I am drowning.

fr.L: L’abîme appelle l’abîme au bruit de {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} cascades ; tous {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} brisants et {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} vagues ont passé sur moi.
fr.B: Un abîme appelle un autre abîme au grondement de {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} chutes d’eau ; toutes {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} vagues et {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} lames ont passé par-dessus ma tête.
fr.R: Tes chutes d’eau grondent, et les eaux profondes s’appellent l’une l’autre. C’est comme si {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} vagues s’écrasaient sur moi, et que je me noyais.

sw.L: Kilindi kinakiita kilindi kwa sauti ya maporomoko {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} ya maji; mawimbi {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} yote na viwimbi {{deity_pronoun:vyako|Vyako}} vimepita juu yangu.
sw.B: Kilindi kimoja kinakiita kingine kwa mngurumo wa maporomoko {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} ya maji; mawimbi {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} yote yanayovunjika na kusukumana yamepita juu ya kichwa changu.
sw.R: Maporomoko {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} ya maji yananguruma, na maji ya vilindi yanaitana. Ni kana kwamba mawimbi {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} yananipiga, nami ninazama.

es.L: Un abismo llama a otro abismo al sonido de {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} cascadas; todas {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} rompientes y {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} olas han pasado sobre mí.
es.B: Un abismo clama a otro al estruendo de {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} cascadas; todas {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} olas que rompen y ruedan me han pasado por encima de la cabeza.
es.R: Tus cascadas rugen, y las aguas profundas se llaman unas a otras. Es como si {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} olas se estrellaran sobre mí, y yo me estuviera ahogando.

vi.L: Vực sâu gọi vực sâu theo tiếng các thác nước của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}; mọi sóng cồn và lượn sóng của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã tràn qua tôi.
vi.B: Vực thẳm này gọi vực thẳm kia giữa tiếng gầm của các thác nước {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}; mọi đợt sóng vỗ và cuộn sóng của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã phủ qua đầu tôi.
vi.R: Các thác nước của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} gầm thét, và những dòng nước sâu gọi nhau. Như thể sóng của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang ập trên tôi, và tôi đang chết đuối.

decisions.choice: deep to deep: the great waters
decisions.reason: The deep (tehom) is the mass of water of Genesis 1:2. In the north the poet hears torrents roaring, and they become a picture of the troubles that overwhelm him.

decisions.choice: your waterfalls
decisions.reason: The word (tsinnor) is rare and may mean a channel or rush of water.

decisions.choice: your breakers, your waves: trouble that God allows
decisions.reason: He calls the waves God's: even his distress is under God's hand (88:8). The words are echoed in Jonah's prayer from the sea (Jonah 2).

decisions.choice: It is as if ... I am drowning
decisions.reason: Readable makes the picture a comparison and says what it means.

source.text: יוֹמָ֤ם׀יְצַוֶּ֬ה יְהוָ֨ה׀חַסְדּ֗וֹ וּ֭בַלַּיְלָה שִׁיר֣וֹ עִמִּ֑י תְּ֝פִלָּ֗ה לְאֵ֣ל חַיָּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: By day YHWH commands his loyal love, and in the night his song [is] with me, a prayer to [the] God of my life.

en.L: By day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commands {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love, and in the night {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} song [is] with me, a prayer to the God of my life.
en.B: By day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sends out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love, and at night {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} song stays with me, a prayer to the God who gives me life.
en.R: During the day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} shows me {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} faithful love. At night I sing to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and pray to God, who keeps me alive.

fr.L: Le jour, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} commande {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} amour loyal, et la nuit {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} chant [est] avec moi, une prière au Dieu de ma vie.
fr.B: Le jour, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} envoie {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} amour fidèle, et la nuit {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} chant reste avec moi, une prière au Dieu qui me donne la vie.
fr.R: Pendant la journée, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} me montre {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} amour fidèle. La nuit, je chante pour {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et je prie Dieu, qui me garde en vie.

sw.L: Mchana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} anaamuru upendo {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} usiokoma, na usiku wimbo {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} [uko] pamoja nami, maombi kwa Mungu wa uhai wangu.
sw.B: Mchana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hutuma upendo {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} usiokoma, na usiku wimbo {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} hukaa pamoja nami, maombi kwa Mungu anayenipa uhai.
sw.R: Mchana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hunionyesha upendo {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} usiokoma. Usiku ninamwimbia na kumwomba Mungu, anayeniweka hai.

es.L: De día {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} envía {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} amor leal, y en la noche {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} canto [está] conmigo, una oración al Dios de mi vida.
es.B: De día {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} envía {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} amor fiel, y de noche {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} canto se queda conmigo, una oración al Dios que me da la vida.
es.R: Durante el día {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me muestra {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} amor fiel. De noche {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} canto y oro a Dios, que me mantiene con vida.

vi.L: Ban ngày {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} truyền tình yêu thương thành tín của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và ban đêm bài ca của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} [ở] với tôi, một lời cầu nguyện dâng lên Đức Chúa Trời của sự sống tôi.
vi.B: Ban ngày {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sai tình yêu thương thành tín của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến, và ban đêm bài ca về {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ở với tôi, một lời cầu nguyện dâng lên Đức Chúa Trời, Đấng ban sự sống cho tôi.
vi.R: Ban ngày {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} bày tỏ cho tôi tình thương không hề thay đổi của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Ban đêm tôi hát cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và cầu nguyện với Đức Chúa Trời, Đấng giữ tôi sống.

decisions.choice: loyal love
decisions.reason: As in 40:11 (chesed).

decisions.choice: commands: sends out, or may he send out
alternatives: May the LORD command his loyal love
decisions.reason: The LORD gives an order and his loyal love goes out like a messenger (compare 43:3). The verb can also be a wish.

decisions.choice: his song: a song about him, sung at night
decisions.reason: "His song" is the song he gives or the song in his praise. Day and night together mean all the time.

decisions.choice: the LORD: the divine name, once in the poem
decisions.reason: The divine name appears only here in Psalms 42-43.

source.text: אוֹמְרָ֤ה׀לְאֵ֥ל סַלְעִי֮ לָמָ֪ה שְׁכַ֫חְתָּ֥נִי לָֽמָּה־קֹדֵ֥ר אֵלֵ֗ךְ בְּלַ֣חַץ אוֹיֵֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: I will say to God my rock, Why have you forgotten me? Why mourning do I walk about in [the] oppression of an enemy?

en.L: I will say to God my rock, "Why have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} forgotten me? Why do I walk about mourning under the oppression of an enemy?"
en.B: I cry out to God, my rock: "Why have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} put me out of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} mind? Why do I walk about dressed in grief while the enemy presses me hard?"
en.R: God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are my rock. So I ask {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, "Why have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} forgotten me? Why am I so sad? Why do my enemies treat me so badly?"

fr.L: Je dirai à Dieu, mon rocher : « Pourquoi m’as-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} oublié ? Pourquoi vais-je en deuil sous l’oppression d’un ennemi ? »
fr.B: Je crie vers Dieu, mon rocher : « Pourquoi m’as-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} chassé de {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} pensée ? Pourquoi dois-je aller vêtu de deuil, pendant que l’ennemi m’écrase ? »
fr.R: Dieu, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es mon rocher. Alors je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} demande : « Pourquoi m’as-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} oublié ? Pourquoi suis-je si triste ? Pourquoi mes ennemis me font-ils tant de mal ? »

sw.L: Nitamwambia Mungu mwamba wangu, "Kwa nini umenisahau? Kwa nini ninatembea nikiomboleza chini ya uonevu wa adui?"
sw.B: Ninamlilia Mungu, mwamba wangu: "Kwa nini umeniondoa mawazoni {{deity_pronoun:mwako|Mwako}}? Kwa nini ninatembea nimevaa huzuni huku adui akinikandamiza?"
sw.R: Mungu, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni mwamba wangu. Kwa hiyo ninakuuliza, "Kwa nini umenisahau? Kwa nini nina huzuni hivi? Kwa nini adui zangu wananitendea vibaya hivi?"

es.L: Diré a Dios, mi roca: «¿Por qué {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} has olvidado de mí? ¿Por qué ando enlutado bajo la opresión del enemigo?».
es.B: Clamo a Dios, mi roca: «¿Por qué me has borrado de {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} mente? ¿Por qué ando vestido de luto mientras el enemigo me oprime?».
es.R: Dios, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} eres mi roca. Por eso {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} pregunto: «¿Por qué {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} has olvidado de mí? ¿Por qué estoy tan triste? ¿Por qué mis enemigos me tratan tan mal?».

vi.L: Tôi sẽ nói với Đức Chúa Trời, vầng đá của tôi: "Sao {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã quên tôi? Sao tôi phải đi lại than khóc dưới sự áp bức của kẻ thù?"
vi.B: Tôi kêu lên cùng Đức Chúa Trời, vầng đá của tôi: "Sao {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} gạt tôi ra khỏi tâm trí {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}? Sao tôi phải đi lại trong áo tang, trong khi kẻ thù ép bức tôi?"
vi.R: Lạy Đức Chúa Trời, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} là vầng đá của tôi. Vậy tôi hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Sao {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã quên tôi? Sao tôi buồn rầu đến thế? Sao kẻ thù lại đối xử tệ với tôi như vậy?"

decisions.choice: my rock: my safe place
decisions.reason: A high rock is a place of safety from enemies (18:3; 31:4).

decisions.choice: mourning: dressed in dark clothes of grief
decisions.reason: The word (qoder) is to be dark or dirty, as mourners were, in sackcloth and ashes (35:14; 38:7).

decisions.choice: the same question in 43:2
decisions.reason: The second question is repeated almost word for word in 43:2, one of the signs that the two psalms are one poem.

source.text: בְּרֶ֤צַח׀בְּֽעַצְמוֹתַ֗י חֵרְפ֥וּנִי צוֹרְרָ֑י בְּאָמְרָ֥ם אֵלַ֥י כָּל־הַ֝יּ֗וֹם אַיֵּ֥ה אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: With a shattering in my bones my foes have taunted me, when they say to me all the day, Where [is] your God?

en.L: With a crushing in my bones my foes taunt me, while they say to me all the day, "Where [is] your God?"
en.B: My foes mock me with a taunt that crushes my bones, while all day long they ask me, "Where is your God?"
en.R: My enemies make fun of me, and it hurts me deep inside, as if my bones were broken. All day long they ask me, "Where is your God?"

fr.L: Avec un broiement dans mes os mes adversaires m’insultent, tandis qu’ils me disent tout le jour : « Où [est] ton Dieu ? »
fr.B: Mes adversaires m’insultent, et leurs moqueries me broient les os, pendant que toute la journée ils me demandent : « Où est ton Dieu ? »
fr.R: Mes ennemis se moquent de moi, et cela me fait mal au plus profond, comme si on me cassait les os. Toute la journée, ils me demandent : « Où est ton Dieu ? »

sw.L: Kwa kusagwa mifupa yangu watesi wangu wananidhihaki, wanaponiambia mchana kutwa, "Mungu wako [yuko] wapi?"
sw.B: Watesi wangu wananidhihaki kwa dhihaka inayoponda mifupa yangu, huku mchana kutwa wakiniuliza, "Mungu wako yuko wapi?"
sw.R: Adui zangu wananidhihaki, na hilo linaniumiza ndani kabisa, kana kwamba mifupa yangu imevunjika. Mchana kutwa wananiuliza, "Mungu wako yuko wapi?"

es.L: Con quebranto en mis huesos me afrentan mis adversarios, mientras me dicen todo el día: «¿Dónde [está] tu Dios?».
es.B: Mis adversarios se burlan de mí con un insulto que me rompe los huesos, mientras todo el día me preguntan: «¿Dónde está tu Dios?».
es.R: Mis enemigos se burlan de mí, y eso me duele en lo más hondo, como si tuviera los huesos rotos. Todo el día me preguntan: «¿Dónde está tu Dios?».

vi.L: Với sự nghiền nát trong xương cốt tôi, những kẻ đối địch tôi chế nhạo tôi, trong khi chúng suốt ngày nói với tôi: "Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi [ở] đâu?"
vi.B: Những kẻ đối địch nhạo báng tôi bằng lời làm nát cả xương cốt tôi, trong khi suốt ngày chúng hỏi tôi: "Đức Chúa Trời của anh ở đâu?"
vi.R: Kẻ thù chế giễu tôi, và điều đó làm tôi đau đớn tận trong lòng, như thể xương tôi bị gãy. Suốt ngày chúng hỏi tôi: "Đức Chúa Trời của anh đâu rồi?"

decisions.choice: a shattering in my bones: pain that goes to the bone
alternatives: as with a sword in my bones
decisions.reason: The word (retsach) is used elsewhere of murder; here it is a deadly blow felt in the bones, the frame of the whole person (6:3).

decisions.choice: Where is your God?
decisions.reason: As in verse 4.

source.text: מַה־תִּשְׁתּ֬וֹחֲחִ֨י׀נַפְשִׁי֮ וּֽמַה־תֶּהֱמִ֪י עָ֫לָ֥י הוֹחִ֣ילִי לֵֽ֭אלֹהִים כִּי־ע֣וֹד אוֹדֶ֑נּוּ יְשׁוּעֹ֥ת פָּ֝נַ֗י וֵֽאלֹהָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Why are you bowed down, my soul, and why are you in turmoil within me? Wait for God, for I will yet give thanks to him, [the] salvation of my face and my God.

en.L: Why are you bowed down, my soul, and why are you in turmoil within me? Wait for God, for I will yet give thanks to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, the salvation of my face and my God.
en.B: Why are you bent so low, my soul? Why this unrest inside me? Wait for God in hope; I will give {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} thanks again, the one who saves me, my God.
en.R: I tell myself: Why are you so sad? Why are you so upset? Keep hoping in God! I will praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} again. He saves me. He is my God.

fr.L: Pourquoi es-tu abattue, mon âme, et pourquoi gémis-tu au-dedans de moi ? Espère en Dieu, car je {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} louerai encore, le salut de ma face et mon Dieu.
fr.B: Pourquoi es-tu si abattue, mon âme ? Pourquoi ce trouble au-dedans de moi ? Espère en Dieu ; je {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} rendrai grâce encore, à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui me sauve, mon Dieu.
fr.R: Je me dis : Pourquoi es-tu si triste ? Pourquoi es-tu si inquiet ? Continue d’espérer en Dieu ! Je {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} louerai encore. Il me sauve. Il est mon Dieu.

sw.L: Mbona umeinama, nafsi yangu, na mbona unafadhaika ndani yangu? Mngojee Mungu, kwa maana bado nitamshukuru {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}, wokovu wa uso wangu na Mungu wangu.
sw.B: Mbona umeinama hivyo, nafsi yangu? Mbona huku kuhangaika ndani yangu? Mngojee Mungu kwa tumaini; nitamshukuru tena, {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} anayeniokoa, Mungu wangu.
sw.R: Ninajiambia: Mbona una huzuni hivyo? Mbona umefadhaika hivyo? Endelea kumtumaini Mungu! Nitamsifu tena. Yeye huniokoa. Yeye ni Mungu wangu.

es.L: ¿Por qué estás abatida, alma mía, y por qué te turbas dentro de mí? Espera en Dios, porque aún {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} daré gracias, la salvación de mi rostro y mi Dios.
es.B: ¿Por qué te doblegas tanto, alma mía? ¿Por qué esta inquietud dentro de mí? Espera en Dios con esperanza; otra vez {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} daré gracias, a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, que me salva, mi Dios.
es.R: Me digo a mí mismo: ¿Por qué estás tan triste? ¿Por qué estás tan preocupado? ¡Sigue esperando en Dios! Otra vez {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} alabaré. Él me salva. Él es mi Dios.

vi.L: Hỡi linh hồn tôi, sao lại cúi rạp xuống, và sao lại xao xuyến trong tôi? Hãy trông đợi Đức Chúa Trời, vì tôi sẽ còn cảm tạ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, là sự cứu rỗi của mặt tôi và là Đức Chúa Trời của tôi.
vi.B: Hỡi linh hồn tôi, sao lại gục ngã đến thế? Sao lại bồn chồn trong tôi? Hãy hy vọng nơi Đức Chúa Trời; tôi sẽ lại cảm tạ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, là Đấng cứu tôi, là Đức Chúa Trời của tôi.
vi.R: Tôi tự nhủ: Sao lại buồn đến thế? Sao lại bối rối đến thế? Hãy cứ hy vọng nơi Đức Chúa Trời! Tôi sẽ lại ca ngợi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Ngài cứu tôi. Ngài là Đức Chúa Trời của tôi.

decisions.choice: my soul: the psalmist speaks to himself
decisions.reason: The refrain is a conversation inside the psalmist: one part of him asks why his soul is so low and urges it to hope. Soul (nefesh) is the whole self, here his own heart.

decisions.choice: bowed down, in turmoil: crushed and restless
decisions.reason: The first verb (shachach) is to be bent low, sunk down; the second (hamah) is the roaring or restlessness of the sea, which the poem pictures in 42:8.

decisions.choice: the salvation of my face: the one who saves me in person
decisions.reason: The plural "salvations" (yeshu'ot) means full rescue. "My face" stands for the person: God is the one who saves him and lifts his face again.

decisions.choice: I tell myself: Why are you ...
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that he is speaking to himself (m1).

decisions.choice: the refrain again
decisions.reason: As in verse 6, but the Hebrew here ends "the salvation of my face and my God"; 43:5 repeats these words exactly.
